title: Approval routing: tool approvals, delegates, timeouts
goal: Route approval requests and decisions between the right approvers, enforce delegation and expiry, and notify the notification dispatcher, using only the cleartext routing metadata.
scope_in: Handler for approval.request and approval.decision hybrid frames using p fields approval_id, agent_id, risk, expires_at, approver (host|owner|any_editor), decision (approve|deny), scope (once|session|always).
Authorisation of deciders: host always; delegated approvers only for requests whose p.approver allows them (owner = workspace owner/admin member in the session, any_editor = any editor).
Pending-approval store with expiry: at expires_at the relay sequences an approval.decision {decision:'deny', scope:'once'} from the server (timeout), once.
First decision wins; later decisions for the same approval_id are ignored with sys.error `forbidden` or a no-op for exact duplicates.
Mute and kick of a requester cancel their pending approvals; agent.exit cancels pending approvals for that agent.
Event to the notification dispatcher (category approval_needed, params agent/session/risk) through a NotifyPort, and sys.notice-free (no display text).
scope_out: The permission engine that decides what needs approval (client).
Agent registry: B057; control commands such as delegating the host: B051.
build_against: FakeSequencer/Fanout/Clock ports, MembershipPort fake with roles, NotifyPort recorder; contracts/fixtures/events/approval.*.json; B011 simulator for host, editor and guest.
interfaces: ApprovalRouter.onRequest(ctx, frame): Promise<Result>; onDecision(ctx, frame): Promise<Result>; sweep(now: Date): Promise<number>
PendingApproval = {approvalId:'apr_…', agentId, requester:'mem_…', risk:'low'|'medium'|'high', approver:'host'|'owner'|'any_editor', expiresAt:string, requestSeq:number}
Redis hash approval:{sid}:{apr} with TTL = expires_at + 60 s
acceptance: approval.request from the host/owner of the agent is sequenced and stored; NotifyPort.approvalNeeded is called exactly once per approval_id even if the frame is retried.

Decision by an editor when approver='host' is rejected `forbidden` and audited; with approver='any_editor' an editor decision is accepted; with 'owner' only owner/admin members of the workspace are accepted.
Viewers never decide; a requester cannot approve their own request unless they are the host.
Two decisions race (approve and deny) -> the one with the lower seq wins, the other gets a no-op error and no second state change.

expires_at in the past on a request is rejected `invalid_frame`; a request with expires_at more than 24 h ahead is clamped by rejecting `invalid_frame`; at expires_at (fake clock) one server deny decision is sequenced exactly once even with two sweepers.
agent.exit or kick of the requester removes pending approvals without emitting a timeout deny.
Decision scope 'always' or 'session' is forwarded as-is; the relay stores no memory of scopes and does not auto-answer future requests.
Pending approvals survive relay restart (Redis restore) and are re-armed with their original expires_at.
tests: approvals.privacy.test.ts: no ct-derived data in store/logs
guardrails: MUST NOT auto-approve anything; the only server-originated decision is deny on expiry.
MUST authorise deciders from live membership; the request's `approver` field narrows who may decide but never widens beyond role rules in CT-RBAC.
MUST NOT read summary, command or cwd from ct, and MUST NOT include them in notifications.
Expiry deny MUST be sequenced exactly once (guard with SET NX on the approval key).
Notification params MUST contain ids and enums only (agent, session, risk).
failure_modes: Sweeper lag -> a late decision after expires_at but before the sweep is rejected as expired; sweeper emits deny afterwards only if no decision exists.
NotifyPort failure -> approval still routed; notification retried by dispatcher outbox; failure counted.
Host disconnected when request arrives -> request is kept; notification is sent; on expiry the deny is still emitted.
